name: If my budget is limited, what are the most important seismic retrofits to do first?

mainEntity.name: If my budget is limited, what are the most important seismic retrofits to do first?

acceptedAnswer.text:
DIRECT ANSWER: With a tight budget, focus first on keeping the building on its foundation—typically foundation bolting and cripple‑wall bracing—before tackling less critical upgrades.

CONTEXT: Earthquake damage is often worst when the entire structure shifts or falls off its foundation. Addressing this basic load path provides substantial risk reduction for relatively modest cost.

KEY FACTORS:
- Foundation anchoring: sill plate bolts, hold‑downs, and proper washers.
- Cripple‑wall bracing with plywood shear panels, correctly nailed.
- Securing heavy, top‑heavy items (water heaters, tall furniture, chimneys).
- Known structural “red flags” identified by an engineer.

PRACTICAL GUIDANCE: Ask your engineer or contractor to mark items as “critical,” “important,” and “optional” on your scope. Complete the critical items now and plan the rest in phases as funds allow.

SOFT POSITIONING: A good retrofit plan can be phased so you get the highest safety benefit from each dollar spent.
acceptedAnswer.description: On a limited budget, prioritize structural basics: properly bolting the house to the foundation and bracing cripple walls, then securing heavy non‑structural items like water heaters. Ask your engineer or contractor to rank work items by safety impact so you can do the highest‑value upgrades first.
